item.title: Shijimi Clam Miso Soup: The Taste of Lake Shinji — Guide
item.description: Lake Shinji, the brackish lake on the edge of Matsue, is Japan’s leading source of yamato-shijimi, small freshwater clams that are the star of the region’s most beloved dish: shijimi miso soup. The tiny black clams give a deep, savoury broth rich in umami, and the soup is a Matsue staple eaten especially at breakfast — and famous throughout Japan as a folk remedy for a hangover, thanks to the ornithine the clams contain.

item.title: Shimane Leisure Guide: Garden Therapy, Lake Cruises & Mythology Trails
item.description: Shimane moves at a slower frequency than Japan’s major tourist circuits. There are no theme parks, no neon-lit shopping districts. What it offers instead — a garden ranked number one in Japan for over two decades, sunsets named among the country’s hundred most beautiful, boat rides through feudal samurai districts, and coastal paths connecting the birthplaces of Japanese mythology — requires patience and rewards it generously.
